findings.description: The surface taxonomy is still not deterministic enough for lock: F001 says to map the existing 8 qa-sufficiency surface classes, while F002 moves mutation out of surfaces into claim_kind and introduces names like cli_human, mcp_tool, and api without pinning the canonical surface_class enum.
findings.recommendation: Pin the exact surface_class values, the total family mapping for each value, and the migration rule for the prior mutation surface before implementation starts.

findings.description: The required-evidence rule uses ambiguous set notation for alternatives, such as screenshot|recording|journey_walk and tool_call_transcript|contract_check, structured_error, so implementers can disagree on whether all classes, any class, or a fallback-specific class is required.
findings.recommendation: Specify required_evidence_classes as an explicit Boolean/minimum-satisfaction expression per surface, consumer, and claim_kind, including when structured_error is required.

findings.description: F005 names completion_auditor enforcement but does not pin the actual close-path integration points in the existing platform, where auditing and plan close are separate concerns; a finding file alone would not guarantee that product-class close is blocked.
findings.recommendation: Require wiring through the real close command/gate path and add an end-to-end close attempt test proving consumer_outcome_unproven blocks product-class closure.

findings.description: The advisory posture for substrate plans is under-specified against the current schemas: objective contracts currently accept only product goal types, substrate plans need not declare contracts, and F005 has an opted_in parameter without a declared schema or frontmatter source.
findings.recommendation: Define where substrate-plan consumer declarations and the opted-in flag live, then test a real mechanical/infra/refactor plan with the same gap warning rather than blocking.

findings.description: Typed-skip evidence and honest in-journey capability-unavailable evidence can share the same structured tuple of availability=unavailable and data_provenance=degraded, yet F004 and F005 require different close outcomes depending on whether a real journey execution also occurred.
findings.recommendation: Pin the structured discriminator used to prove real journey execution separately from source-unavailable typed-skip evidence, without relying on prose notes.
